assessment_summary: I validated the installation against the supplied guide in the same container. (1) Toolchain inspection confirmed the guide's prerequisites (yarn 1.22.22 via npm global install, Node v22.17.0). (2) File inspection of /workspace confirmed package.json (next 16.3.4, output:'export', distDir:'build'), a complete node_modules (557 packages from the successful yarn install via registry.npmjs.org, after the abandoned registry.yarnpkg.com attempt), and a complete build/ export matching the guide's description (192 HTML pages across de/, en/, fit-standards/, resources/, search-data JSON, robots.txt, _next assets; every asset referenced in index.html exists in the export; expected title and metadata present). (3) I verified live behavior for both documented runtime modes: `yarn dev` started the Next.js dev server on port 3000 and served /, /de/, /en/, /fit-standards/, /resources/meta/ with HTTP 200 and the expected title; `yarn start` (npx serve@latest build) served the production export on port 3000 with HTTP 200 on all key routes, CSS/JS assets, and search-data, correct per-locale html lang attributes, and proper 404 handling for unknown paths. (4) All test servers were stopped and port 3000 confirmed free, leaving the environment clean. Limitations: browser-level client-side interactivity was not tested (HTTP + prerendered HTML evidence used, appropriate for a static export); no .env.local was created, but the Plausible analytics variables have documented defaults so no functional impact. The abandoned-then-recovered yarn registry switch left no unresolved gaps since the final node_modules is complete and both runtime modes operate. These observations demonstrate the installation is complete and operational per the guide.
